 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Hawks won 128-81, their largest blowout in franchise history , per the AP. The 47-point margin topped the old record of 46 .
 The scoreboard grabs the eye, but the more interesting part is how it happened. Atlanta forced 14 first-half turnovers, which led to 15 points on the break and a 25-point cushion at halftime. By the end, Peachtree Hoops counted 17 Hawks steals against 27 Charlotte turnovers, good for 25 points the other way.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The offense wasn't an afterthought either. Atlanta shot 50.5 percent, all five starters reached double figures, and Jalen Johnson filled the sheet with 19 points, eight assists and seven rebounds. Aaron Wiggins added 19 off the bench on 7-of-9 shooting. CJ McCollum, per Yahoo Sports , scored 11 in the first quarter to set the tone.
 Charlotte handed them plenty of help in rough home opener
 Context matters here. The Hornets played without Kon Knueppel, Coby White and Grant Williams, and it was their first home game since trading LaMelo Ball, a move that hasn't gone over well with the fan base . The crowd let them hear about it as the game slipped away. Charlotte went 2-for-15 from three in the opening quarter.
 The Hornets played without Kon Knueppel, Coby White and Grant WilliamsJoe Murphy / Getty Images
 None of that takes away from Atlanta's record setting game. But it's a reason to hold the confetti until the Hawks show this against a healthier opponent.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Houston arrives with tired legs and perfect record
 That test comes fast. The Rockets, also 2-0, visit State Farm Arena in what Sports Mole called the game of the night . Houston is playing its third game in four nights after edging San Antonio on Friday, while Atlanta has played two in that span.
 The same preview credits the Hawks with the best defensive rating on tonight's slate, 98.6 points allowed per 100 possessions, against 111.1 for Houston. Reed Sheppard sat Friday with a knee issue, and his status for tonight was still uncertain at last check.
 Also read: Oklahoma City Thunder are the NBA's cream of the crop once again 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Houston has Alperen Sengun, Kevin Durant and Amen Thompson, so this won't resemble a Charlotte-style rout. The Rockets can score on anybody. The question is whether Atlanta's pressure still bites when the other side has real shot-makers and a little experience closing games.
 Peachtree Hoops described Friday's defense as part of an identity the Hawks are still trying to form. That's the right frame. Two games prove very little, but they do show a preference: make teams uncomfortable, run in transition, and let a deep rotation do the rest.
 If that holds against Houston, people will stop calling this a hot start and begin treating it like a plan.
